items.title: Nvidia Halts Sales to Southeast Asia as U.S. Tightens China Restrictions
items.summary: Nvidia has halted chip shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after Washington issued a new rule requiring companies in those countries to obtain licenses before buying advanced AI chips. The move is meant to close a remote-access loophole that let Chinese firms tap GPU computing power through the region.
items.why_it_matters: It shows the US is widening its chip-export dragnet beyond China itself, directly threatening the Southeast Asian data-center buildout that has become a key channel for AI compute.

items.title: S&P Says It May Downgrade Nvidia’s Ratings on Governance Worries
items.summary: S&P Global Ratings is considering cutting Nvidia's credit rating by one notch, citing rising management and governance risk following the departure and subsequent return of CEO Jensen Huang. The warning ties the chipmaker's financial standing directly to boardroom turmoil at the center of the global AI buildout.
items.why_it_matters: Nvidia's credit rating underpins financing for much of the AI data-center boom, so a governance-driven downgrade could ripple through borrowing costs across the sector.

items.title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
items.summary: The FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites in orbit as part of its 'Starmind' initiative, the agency's first approval of its kind. Google and Blue Origin are also pursuing orbital AI data centers, but SpaceX is now first to clear this regulatory hurdle.
items.why_it_matters: It's the first regulatory green light for putting AI compute in orbit, a frontier that could reshape where data centers get built and how power and cooling constraints on Earth are sidestepped.

items.title: [AINews] Gemini 4 Neon marks GDM's full return as a Frontier Lab
items.summary: Google DeepMind's new Gemini 4 Neon model beats rival models Astra and Fable on the LiveBench benchmark, and cuts the runtime of a TypeScript/Rust coding benchmark by 48.6%. Latent Space's AINews digest frames the release as marking Google DeepMind's full return to the frontier-lab tier.
items.why_it_matters: A new model that measurably outperforms top rivals on independent benchmarks reshuffles the competitive order among frontier labs.

items.title: New York bans AI toys, including those using internet to talk to children
items.summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a five-year ban on manufacturing and selling AI chatbot toys, including talking stuffed animals and internet-connected dolls that converse with children. The state's attorney general said she would 'not hesitate to enforce' the law, which follows research from Common Sense Media documenting safety failures such as exposure to inappropriate content.
items.why_it_matters: It's one of the first outright state bans on a category of consumer AI product, aimed squarely at child safety, and could set a template for other states.

items.title: JPMorgan Sees $450 Billion AI Debt Blitz in 2027 Before Plateau
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase analysts forecast that companies will tap public high-grade debt markets for $450 billion in 2027 to finance AI-related capital expenditures, even as they see a growth plateau looming further down the road for the industry.
items.why_it_matters: It's a concrete number on just how much debt financing the AI buildout is expected to require, and a warning that the growth underpinning it may not last indefinitely.

items.title: US Genesis Mission Looks to AI to Accelerate Science
items.summary: One year after launch, the US Department of Energy's Genesis Mission has grown to nearly 300 AI-driven research projects spanning energy, biology, advanced manufacturing and national security. DOE Undersecretary for Science Dario Gil described using AI to simulate the power grid 1,000 times faster and to accelerate nuclear and fusion development, with a goal of doubling US R&D productivity within a decade.
items.why_it_matters: It's a concrete look at how a national government is trying to harness AI to speed up science itself, at a scale that could affect energy and nuclear research timelines.

items.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
items.summary: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to block Character.AI's bankruptcy sale, which would include the private chat histories of more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including 2.1 million registered to minors. The AGs say the sale of such sensitive personal data should not proceed as part of the Chapter 11 process.
items.why_it_matters: It raises the question of whether a failed AI company's most sensitive asset, years of users' intimate chat logs, can simply be auctioned off as a bankruptcy asset.

items.title: ElevenLabs in Early Talks for Funding at $33 Billion Value
items.summary: ElevenLabs, which builds AI voice models and agents, is in early discussions for a new funding round targeting a $33 billion valuation, according to people familiar with the matter.
items.why_it_matters: A valuation of that size for a voice-AI specialist signals how much investor appetite remains for AI infrastructure bets even as broader AI stocks wobble.

items.title: Google releases Cogentic papers on integer factorization, discrete logs and more
items.summary: Google published a collection of research papers, under the name 'Cogentic,' covering integer factorization, discrete logarithms and related computational problems, posted to its google-research GitHub repository. The release drew heavy engagement on Hacker News, with 452 points and 338 comments.
items.why_it_matters: Integer factorization and discrete logs underpin much of modern cryptography, so new research results in this area from a major lab draw outsized attention from both researchers and security practitioners.
